title: Billing ops: deferred overages, credit failover, and post-contract settlement flow
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers and sales are requesting flexible handling for multi-factor billing edge cases during contract amendments and security questionnaire delays. Current systems incorrectly apply credits, create duplicate refunds, or fail to defer overage charges when customers request temporary service hold (security review, data residency onboarding). Scope: define deterministic business rules, reconciliation logic, UI/UX for finance ops, and automation to reduce manual interventions.
updates: 2026-01-27: Kickoff with Finance, Sales, Legal, and Billing infra. Captured 12 canonical edge cases from enterprise accounts (SaaS security delay, region migration, commitment reduction mid-cycle, multi-team account credits).
2026-02-10: Prototype business rules drafted — three modes: immediate-credit, deferred-charge (60-day hold), and settlement-only (manual approval). Shared with Finance for feedback.

2026-02-24: Engineering spike complete; identified webhook idempotency race when invoice adjustments and metering events are processed in parallel. Mitigation: sequence tokens for invoice adjustments and a tombstone record for reversed credits.

2026-03-03: Legal requested audit trail addition for contract amendments referencing security questionnaire exceptions (PCI/P1). Added requirement to surface KMS key ID and signer in refund metadata for Private deployments.

2026-03-12: UX wireframes (console) for Credit Failover workflow validated with BillingOps. Decision: surface triage action in invoice detail page and batch CSV for large settlements. Moving to implementation phase.
Pending: implement canary, prepare runbook, and schedule shadow reconciliation for 2 cycles before full rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New business rules implemented and covered by unit/integration tests: immediate-credit, deferred-charge, settlement-only
A2: Refunds and credits include immutable audit metadata: contract_version, security_questionnaire_id (if present), signer, KMS_key_id
A3: No double-credit or duplicate refund observed in 3-day stress test with synthetic metering bursts
A4: Console shows explicit invoice state transitions and provides one-click batch settlement export (CSV) for Finance
A5: Reconciliation job produces <0.01% mismatch rate vs. ledger after two billing cycles in shadow mode
tasks: T1: Finalize canonical edge-case matrix (Finance + Sales) — Maya
T2: Implement sequence token and tombstone records in billing pipeline — ENG
T3: Add audit metadata fields to refund API and enforcements in Private deployment — ENG + Security
T4: Console: invoice detail UI for manual triage and batch settlement export — PM + Design + ENG
T5: Write e2e reconciliation test harness and synthetic load generator — ENG
T6: Create ops runbook and SLA for manual settlements and critical path escalations — Finance + Support
T7: Coordinate rollout with Sales enablement for contract amendment playbooks — PM + Sales
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal testing + e2e reconciliation in sandbox accounts (2 weeks)
Stage 2: Shadow reconciliation for select enterprise accounts (2 billing cycles)
Stage 3: Canary enablement for 5% of invoices with manual review flag
Stage 4: Full rollout with automated failover rules and ops runbook published
notes: Trade-offs discussed: fully automated rules reduce ops load but increase risk of incorrectly applying credits for disputed usage — leaning toward conservative default (deferred-charge) with opt-in automation for low-risk accounts.
Security constraint: Private deployments require signed refund metadata; coordinate with KMS team to expose key identifiers to finance UI without leaking secrets.
Follow-up: build analytics to classify high-risk invoices (large credits, cross-region usage) for preemptive review.
